The three values are not isolated. Detail clarity affects the fine detail of the result. Background brightness is the offset value that is used to add or subtract the background. These two settings will result in the change of the total brightness. For that reason, the total brightness may also need to be adjusted.

\tWeighted Average method produces a soft fusion result but may miss detail. This method often gives superior results to FFDSSD method with deep stacks, such as images produced by microscopy. It is worth noting that images to be processed must be in Z order (closest to furthest or furthest to closest with the microscope objective lens relative to sample on the stage).\n\tMaximum Contrast method is similar with weighted average method, and the input images must be in Z order as well. The difference is that the maximum contrast method may loose some detail though what detail is preserved will be sharper. Maximum contrast method is a preferred method of EDF.\n\tFFDSSD is a method that does filtering in the frequency domain using Fast Fourier transform (FFT) and does synthesis in the space domain. FFDSSD can be used for images having misalignment. Users can manually or automatically select reference images to make input images aligned.

1. The report template use placeholders to represent various content to be replaced.
2. {{YYYY}}{{mm}}{{DD}}{{HH}}{{MM}}{{SS}} is a time placeholder which represent Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second respectively. {{LD}}{{SD}} respectively represents a long date and a short date.
3. The image in this template whose title or description of alternative text is {{IP}} will be regarded as the image placeholder, the number indicates the image sequence, such as {{IP1}}, {{IP2}}, etc.
4. A table filled with content of {{MT}} will be regarded as the measurement table placeholder. {{MH}} represent the table header.
5. {{MT.i.x.y}} is the placeholder for the content of the measurement table. i is the index of the image, x is the row index of the item in the measurement table，y is the column index of the item in the measurement table. If there is only one image in the report, i should be set to 1. The start value of i, x, y is 1. For example, {{MT.1.2.3}} represent the content of the item, which is at row 2, column 3 position of measurement table of image 1. When x is a negative value, it indicates the xth row of the last number, for example, {{MT.1.-2.3}} represents the content of the penultimate second row and the third column of the measurement table of the first picture.
6. {{LU}}{{AU}}{{SU}} are placeholders for units of length, angle and area, respectively. {{lu}}{{au}}{{su}} mean abbreviations.
7. When the Word/Excel report is generated, image placeholders will be replaced by corresponding content. The replacement of multiple pictures will depend on the image selection order in the thumbnail UI.
8. Word/Excel version must be 2007 or above.
